name: Cicera
description: Cicera (also known as Cicera Bigia or Ciccera Biccera) is an Italian fishing card game closely related to Scopa and Scopone, played in the province of Brescia using a unique 52-card Bresciane deck. The game is the reason why Bresciane playing cards are made with 52 cards rather than the standard Italian 40 cards.

content.text: Cicera (also known as Cicera Bigia or Ciccera Biccera) is an Italian fishing card game closely related to Scopa and Scopone, played in the province of Brescia using a unique 52-card Bresciane deck. The game is the reason why Bresciane playing cards are made with 52 cards rather than the standard Italian 40 cards.

Country/Region of Origin: Province of Brescia, Italy
Time Period: Historical game with long tradition
Historical Development: The game influenced the local card manufacturing tradition, requiring 52-card decks rather than the standard 40-card Italian packs. Related to Scopa and Scopone but with local Bresciane characteristics.
Cultural Significance: The reason Bresciane cards have 52 cards instead of 40. Similar to how Trevisane cards have 52 cards for ScarabociÃ³n.

Minimum Players: 4
Maximum Players: 4
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Yes, fixed partnerships (partners opposite)

Type: Bresciane 52-card pack
Number of Decks: 1
Jokers: Not included
Cards: Re (King), Cavallo (Horse), Fante (Jack), 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, A in each suit
Alternative: Standard international 52-card pack can be used

Bresciane 52-card deck (or standard 52-card pack)
Score sheet
Table space

Cards per Player: 12 cards each
Table Cards: 4 cards face-up to center
Dealing Pattern: Anticlockwise
Redeal: If 3 or 4 Aces appear in initial table cards, reshuffle and redeal
